title: A file share
summary: A folder on the old PC that phones and laptops can open. Samba. No NAS required.

start.body: A file share is a folder phones and laptops open like a USB drive on the network. You don't buy a Synology for a folder of photos. SSH in first.

folder.body: Make a folder: sudo mkdir -p /srv/share. Keep it simple. One share, named something obvious like photos or house.

samba.body: Install: sudo apt install samba. In /etc/samba/smb.conf add a [photos] block with path = /srv/share, browsable = yes, read only = no, valid users = youruser. Then: sudo smbpasswd -a youruser && sudo systemctl restart smbd.

open.body: Windows: \\lab-address\photos. Mac: smb://lab-address/photos. Phone: Files / My Files with the same address and share password.

choices.label: It opens and I can write
I can see it but can't write

done.body: Leave it. Use the folder. Don't expose Samba to the internet. A backup of this folder is the next job when you're ready.

chown.body: Linux folder owner is usually the culprit. Run: sudo chown youruser:youruser /srv/share — then try again.

ufw.body: If ufw is on: sudo ufw allow Samba. Confirm with sudo ufw status. Still house network only.
